doc.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Classical-only music training in Cuba
summary: Cuban musical training was strictly classical, ignoring Cuban and Afro-Cuban music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: 1980, was strictly classical. Everything was about Mozart, Tchaikovsky, Beethoven, Bach. Nothing about Afro-Cuban music or Cuban music in general.

So the analogy that occurs to me in the United States about the time you were a teenager would have been rock music, that would have been the popular music for the most part that jazz had been really popular but sort of displanted by rock music. So what was the popular music in Cuba, like when you were let’s say seventeen?
